briefing.headline: UK debates Brexit benefits as US midterms reshape Congress
briefing.overview: The UK prime minister will claim Brexit has failed ahead of an EU summit, while the US sees a Democratic surge after the midterms and legal battles over a Trump‑linked development. Both sides face pressure from parties and interest groups.

stories.title: Burnham says Brexit ‘has not worked’
stories.what_happened: Prime Minister Andy Burnham will argue that the UK’s post‑Brexit arrangement has delivered fewer benefits than expected and will propose a new deal with the EU. The speech is scheduled for Monday ahead of an EU summit.
stories.why_it_matters: The claim touches on the constitutional role of the executive in foreign policy and the political debate over devolution of powers to the EU. It also illustrates how the government frames policy success to the electorate.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Burnham’s supporters say a revised EU deal could boost GDP by 0.4% and restore trade benefits.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Opponents warn that renegotiating may undermine sovereignty and delay Brexit reforms.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative commentators claim the speech admits a failure of the Brexit project.

key_term.definition: The powers the Prime Minister and Cabinet have to act without parliamentary approval in certain areas.

stories.exam_use: Use as evidence in an essay on the executive’s role in shaping foreign policy and its political limits.

stories.title: AI minister opens Hay Festival
stories.what_happened: The UK’s first dedicated Minister for Artificial Intelligence will open the Hay Festival Winter Weekend with a discussion on AI’s future. The event highlights the new ministerial post.
stories.why_it_matters: Creates a case study of how the executive creates new departments to address emerging policy areas, linking to the constitutional principle of ministerial responsibility.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Tech advocates say the role shows proactive governance on innovation.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Skeptics worry the post may duplicate existing digital ministries.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Labour voices question whether AI regulation will protect workers.

key_term.definition: The duty of ministers to answer to Parliament for their department’s actions.

stories.exam_use: Cite when discussing how new policy challenges lead to changes in the structure of government.

stories.title: Rewilding charity launches match‑funding appeal
stories.what_happened: A rewilding charity announced a £20,000 match‑funding campaign to restore 1,200 acres in the Cambrian Mountains. Donations will be doubled by a corporate partner.
stories.why_it_matters: Illustrates how pressure groups mobilise public support and funding to influence environmental policy, a key aspect of interest‑group politics.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Environmentalists claim the scheme will boost biodiversity and rural economies.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Local landowners worry increased rewilding could restrict farming activities.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservative voices caution against public‑private partnerships that may bypass parliamentary scrutiny.

key_term.definition: An organised group that seeks to influence public policy without seeking electoral office.

stories.exam_use: Use as a contemporary example when evaluating the impact of interest groups on policy making.

stories.title: Democrats gain after US midterm rout
stories.what_happened: The 2026 midterm elections resulted in a significant Democratic gain in the House, reshaping the balance of power ahead of a potential shutdown. The outcome also sparked internal GOP debates over leadership.
stories.why_it_matters: Shows how electoral outcomes affect party dynamics and legislative agendas, linking to the US Constitution’s separation of powers.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Democrats say the win reflects public rejection of the President’s policies.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Republicans claim the results are a temporary backlash and warn of over‑reach.

perspectives.label: From the left
perspectives.text: Progressives argue the gains will enable more ambitious reforms.

key_term.definition: The political party that holds the most seats in a legislative chamber.

stories.exam_use: Reference when discussing how party control influences legislative priorities in the US Congress.

stories.title: Trump attacks court halt to golf project
stories.what_happened: Former President Donald Trump condemned a judge’s two‑week injunction that stopped work on his Washington golf development and announced plans to appeal. He described the court as “in a terrible state of disrepair”.
stories.why_it_matters: Highlights tensions between the executive and judiciary, a core feature of the US constitutional system of checks and balances.

perspectives.label: Supporters argue
perspectives.text: Trump’s base view the injunction as political interference with private property rights.

perspectives.label: Critics argue
perspectives.text: Legal analysts say the judge acted within judicial authority to enforce environmental regulations.

perspectives.label: From the right
perspectives.text: Conservatives warn the decision reflects judicial activism.

key_term.definition: The power of courts to assess the legality of legislative and executive actions.

stories.exam_use: Use as a case study of judicial review in an essay on the separation of powers.

compare.uk: UK courts interpret statutes and can strike down secondary legislation, but do not have the power of judicial review over primary legislation.
compare.us: US courts can invalidate both federal statutes and executive actions through judicial review, as seen in Trump’s challenge to the injunction.
compare.insight: The contrast shows a stronger check on legislative power in the US, reflecting a more robust separation of powers.

ideas_lens.text: Burnham’s proposal for a new EU deal reflects liberal ideas of cooperation and free trade championed by thinkers like Adam Smith, while the US midterm shift illustrates liberal emphasis on representative government and civil rights.

exam_question.question: Assess the extent to which the executive can shape foreign policy in the UK and the US, using recent examples.
exam_question.tip: Compare Burnham’s EU deal proposal with the US President’s influence over judicial appointments and policy direction.
